item.description:
Ask Cove, now much more capable

  • Ask big questions across your mail. With Mail search on, Cove searches Gmail, reads up to 100 matching emails, cites its sources and tells you how much it covered. Searches for a topic no longer come back empty.
  • “Brief me on today” summarizes your schedule, invitations awaiting a reply and the emails that need you.
  • “Reply saying Thursday works” drafts a reply to the open email in your voice and leaves it for your review. Existing drafts are never replaced unless you ask.
  • Tell Cove to remember or forget things about you; your memories now shape every AI draft and answer.
  • Ask about a contact to see their address and your recent conversations, straight from your mail.
  • New emails and introductions drafted from chat can check your real calendar availability.

Nothing is sent, archived or deleted without you. Cloud sync remains optional; mobile access and push notifications are not available yet.

Your AI keys stay put

  • Fixes an issue in 0.1.47 where AI provider and TypeSafe keys could disappear the first time Cove used them, so Jev and AI writing asked for a key that had just been saved.
  • Settings now confirms a TypeSafe key was actually stored before showing “Credentials saved”.

If you used 0.1.47, re-enter your TypeSafe key and any AI provider API keys once in Settings. Your Google connection, mail and learned voice were not affected.

An assistant that writes like you

  • Cove can learn your writing voice once from your sent mail. AI drafts, replies and introductions then sound like you, across your accounts and, with cloud sync on, your other Macs.
  • Ask Cove to “make an intro between Ana and Luis” or “email Carlos about Friday”. It finds them in your contacts, writes the draft in your voice and opens it for review — nothing is sent.
  • Ask Cove now reads the whole conversation, and a missing TypeSafe key takes you straight to the right setting.
  • Conversations show each email as its own card. Reply has a Reply all option, labels open a searchable list, and the Inbox has an Unread filter.
  • Connect Google Calendar in one step with your existing Google sign-in.
  • AI and TypeSafe keys move to protected storage that stays on this Mac, with optional Touch ID in Settings → Privacy.
  • Reconnecting reuses mail already saved on your Mac instead of downloading it again.

Only a description of your writing style is saved, never your emails. Cloud sync remains optional; mobile access and push notifications are not available yet.
